headline: Senator Maria Cantwell has proposed a hotline between Washington and Beijing so a serious AI accident does not turn into a security crisis.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the framework was released on 7 Oct 2026, before the window, and it is a proposal, not law.
importance_line: A direct line to China could help stop a misread AI accident from escalating, which matters to the public and to governments, but it is one senator's proposal, she does not chair the committee, and nothing is enacted.
summary: IANS reports that Sen. Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, proposed a secure US-China channel modelled on the Cold War Washington-Moscow hotline, as one of six points in an AI governance framework she released on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026. It follows our 5 Oct 2026 edition's report that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expected a US-China channel for AI incidents; the framework also calls for federal safety standards and independent audits before release, and needs further legislative or executive action to bind anyone.
notes: Read at IANS (own wire text). The Hans India carries the same copy. Roll Call and PYMNTS confirm the framework and that it has no legislative text. Earlier story: our 5 Oct 2026 edition, item 2 under Politics and government (Axios interview of 3 Oct 2026, Digitimes). Stale: event 7 Oct 2026.
